protections: Entry-name containment: every path derived from an archive entry name (regular file, directory, or link destination) must stay inside the install destination before any filesystem effect; archives.go:26 builds dstPath with filepath.Join(h.dest, h.normalizePath(f.NameInArchive)) and archives.go:28/34/43/58 all use it with no containment check.

Symlink-target containment: a symlink entry's target must resolve inside the install destination, with relative targets resolved against the link's own directory, before the link is created; archives.go:41-47 creates f.LinkTarget verbatim.

Facade-wide containment: every extractor that Unarchiver.getUnarchiver dispatches to must apply the same containment, not only the tar/zip handler reached through archives.Extractor.Extract (unarchive.go:58-101, archives.go:104-113).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: filepath.Join already normalises '..' and absolute names, so a guard on the raw f.NameInArchive (or on a plain string prefix) looks sufficient and needs no normalisation step.
packages legitimately ship relative and dangling symlinks (libfoo.so.1 -> libfoo.so.1.2.3, with the target appearing later in the archive), so the symlink branch must keep creating them.

macOS-only route that mounts the image with hdiutil and copies the mounted volume with an external copy helper, not archive entries handled by archives.Extractor; the published fix stays in archives.go.
macOS-only and delegated to pkgutil --expand-full: the expanded payload is not an archive entry and the published fix targeted the archives handler.
hardlink entries are silently dropped today (archives.go:48) and the advisory is about symlink following, so there is nothing to guard.
the decompressor's output name is already reduced by filepath.Base in getUnarchiver (unarchive.go:59), so the join at archives.go:129 cannot escape dest.

masking: archives.go:28 creates parent directories (and archives.go:34 the entry directory) outside dest before any check, so a fix placed only at the write (archives.go:58) leaves the directory side effect observable only once the file write is blocked.

pkg/installpackage/check_file.go:130 stat and :143 chmod follow a link planted under the package dir, and pkg/installpackage/copy.go:14 writes to is.copyDir; these are reachable only while T2 leaves the planting step in place.
T7's hardlink branch only exists once os.Link support is added beside the symlink branch; today archives.go:48 drops every LinkTarget entry that is not a symlink.

conflicts.what: A withinDest rule on symlink targets must still create relative and dangling in-dest links; resolving targets with filepath.EvalSymlinks/os.Stat (or rejecting every symlink entry) satisfies T2 while breaking the packages T4 protects (archives.go:43, check_file.go:182-187 builds and creates relative links).

fairness_risks: Packages legitimately ship relative symlinks, including dangling ones whose target is created later in the same tar (libfoo.so.1 -> libfoo.so.1.2.3); any rule that requires the target to already exist refuses a legitimate archive.
An absolute symlink whose target is inside the install directory must still be accepted; a rule banning all absolute targets is over-broad.
Archives written on Windows use backslashes as separators and normalizePath deliberately rewrites them (archives.go:83-90); refusing backslash names refuses legitimate archives.

Entry names that merely contain '..' as a substring (foo..tar.gz), or that start with './', must still extract; a substring ban is over-broad while the correct rule is lexical containment of the joined path.
Directory entries (archives.go:33-39) and their creation must keep working; a rule applied only to regular-file writes leaves the MkdirAll side effect at archives.go:28 open.
aqua cp deliberately writes outside the install tree (pkg/controller/cp/copy.go:12, pkg/installpackage/copy.go:14); a blanket no-write-outside-dest rule must not be applied to that path.

design.why: T1 and T2 are two guards in the same function that are each individually bypassable: with only the entry-name containment, an archive plants link -> /etc and a later entry named link/passwd passes the lexical check and is written through the link at archives.go:58; with only the symlink-target containment, a plain ../../x entry still escapes at archives.go:26/58. So the solver must make two independent judgements, and the second is one a report about path traversal does not force. T5 and T6 are the other two extractors the same facade dispatches to (unarchive.go:66-92), each protected by a strong and different dismissal - a mounted volume copied with an external helper versus a payload expanded by pkgutil - and each needs its own guard because osfile.Copy (osfile/copy.go:12-16) and pkgutil (pkg.go:32) never see the handler. T4 is the coupled must-keep-working value at the very site of T2: relative and dangling in-dest symlinks are a normal package shape, so the natural over-broad fix (reject symlink entries, or resolve targets with EvalSymlinks) fails a compatibility test that MiMo-style solvers typically trip on. That gives at least one deepseek-type (T5/T6) and one mimo-type (T4) with three different dismissal arguments. It beats a T1+T3 design, which one correctly placed containment check closes, and a T5+T6 design, which has no in-file depth and repeats the same macOS-only dismissal twice. T7 and T8 are optional sixth/seventh injection-room traps if more depth is wanted (hardlink branch; a decompress writer that depends on the base() at unarchive.go:59).
